claim: For one-pass SGD with a constant learning rate on linear regression whose features and target have power-law spectra, the best batch-size schedule for a fixed data budget depends on task difficulty: on easy tasks the batch should grow throughout training, while on hard tasks it should stay at the minimum for almost all of training and grow only in a short final phase, and either schedule reaches the best rate one-pass SGD can achieve without decaying the learning rate. Supported only if discrete SGD runs using the derived schedules show final loss scaling with data size at the predicted minimax rate D^(-s*beta/(1+s*beta)) in an easy-task setting and at D^(-s) in a hard-task setting; if, restricted to two-stage schedules, the optimal switch for hard tasks comes after nearly all the data with the remaining fraction shrinking as a power of D; and if a constant learning rate with such a schedule matches cosine and warmup-stable-decay learning-rate schedules in final loss.

experiments: Set up the theory. Setup: one-pass SGD on feature-space linear regression with power-law capacity exponent beta and source exponent s, approximated by an SDE whose loss follows a functional scaling law: excess risk = T^(-s) (signal learning in intrinsic time T) + an integral of a forgetting kernel over noise injected at rate eta*sigma^2 / b(t). Minimise final loss over the schedule b(t) and horizon T subject to total data D = integral of b(t) and b(t) >= B_min. Result (theorems): easy tasks (s >= 1 - 1/beta) favour b(t) ~ B_max (T - t + 1)^(-gamma) growing throughout; hard tasks favour B_min for all but a vanishing fraction (T - T1)/T ~ D^(-(1-1/beta-s)/(2-1/beta)) of training, with loss ~ D^(-s); in the two-stage class, easy tasks prefer the large batch throughout and hard tasks a late switch with D - P* ~ D^gamma.

Check the predicted rates with discrete SGD. Setup: easy task s = 1, beta = 2 and hard task s = 0.4, beta = 2, sigma = 1, learning rate 5e-4, schedules built from the theorem and discretised, data sizes 6,346-137,693. Result: final loss against D follows D^(-s*beta/(1+s*beta)) in the easy regime and D^(-s) in the hard regime (shown on log-log plots); with s = 0.3, beta = 1.5, the theorem-derived schedule at constant learning rate gives a final loss comparable to cosine and warmup-stable-decay schedules (figure).

Note the gap between theory and experiments. Setup: the theory assumes SGD with a constant learning rate, while all LLM runs use AdamW, 1,000 warmup steps and, in an extension, cosine decay; the large-scale MoE runs use a private dataset; most LLM comparisons are single curves read off figures. With cosine decay (50M and 0.5B dense) catch-up and the late-switch advantage persist approximately but merging slows near the end, which the authors attribute to intrinsic time advancing more slowly. The constant-LR + batch schedule matching cosine and WSD in the 50M model used a heuristic, untuned schedule (2x at 70%, 4x at 80%, 8x at 90% of tokens).
